Needs changes before merge.

The picked seam has a separate check for Control and Wear compensation. The new tests pass. No code defect was found in this review.

### Requested before merge

1. `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs:347`: Complete the required heavy-lane validation and record the results in the PR body. The body lists only the quick gate and clippy. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches every heavy target in `motion` and `app` (241 planned steps). Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head. Name the lanes and their results in the body. Fix any failures before the PR becomes ready. Current upstream [AGENTS.md:628-636](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/878d4101a/AGENTS.md#L628-L636) requires these results. The quick gate does not run the ignored heavy tests.

### Results merged with main

All checks ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3350`. No GitHub runner was used.

- PR head: `bc1c6428b7071d740fd19725df24c4d9106a261f`.
- Main: `878d4101a`. The trial merge was clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 145 steps passed, 0 failed, 41.1 minutes. The gate built the motion and mapped app test targets with `--no-run`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed, 4 minutes 44 seconds.
- Heavy lanes: `motion` and `app` were planned but not run. The PR body gives no result for them. They are not a pass.
- Light lane: not run.

### Extra suites run

No extra fixture or importer suite applies. The diff changes no test data, fixture, golden, importer, kernel, or UI file. The quick gate ran both changed integration suites and the motion unit tests. There are no moved goldens to compare.

### Safety mutations

Each guard was disabled only in the local review tree. Each source file was restored before the green check. The tracked tree is clean.

| Disabled guard | Test | Red result | Restored result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collinear first and last cuts | `a_compensated_pick_on_a_sharp_corner_is_refused_by_name_not_moved` | 1 failed, exit 101 | 1 passed, exit 0 |
| Part vertex / parallel edge | `machining2d::contour_comp_pick::tests::a_straight_centre_chord_over_a_part_vertex_is_refused_by_name` | 1 failed, exit 101 | 1 passed, exit 0 |

The first mutation lost the named start-point refusal. The existing square-offset check still refused Control. The second mutation accepted the synthetic part-vertex seam. These were test assertion failures, not build failures.

143 suite steps: 1722 tests passed; 66 tests ignored. Ignored tests are not counted as passed.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head bc1c6428b7071d740fd19725df24c4d9106a261f.

Verdict: no blocker found. I changed no label. Under the safety floor, this read relies on the build and gate results of the author and the reviewer. I did not build.

### 1. Picked start under control compensation

- Before: `pick_ring` refused each pick when `compensation.in_control()` (old `contour_start.rs:75-82`).
- Now: the refusal is removed. `seat` (`contour_start.rs:352-368`) starts the ring at the projection of the pick. It does not use `seam_mid_run`. The lead-in, the lead-out and the span go through the same code as the default seam: `keep_cut` and `lead_fit` (legal room), `lead_held` (`contour.rs:196-200`), the door (`contour_comp.rs:59-90`) and `push_span` (`contour_comp.rs:176-326`).
- The only new code in the path is `picked_seam` (`contour_comp_pick.rs:38-95`), called at `contour_comp.rs:208-211` only when `picked` is `Some`. It adds refusals. It does not change a move.
- These existing checks stay in force for a picked ring: straight lead moves (no arc), lead length at least the tool radius, closed ring, room law (`room::corners`, `room::neck`, `room::arcs`), the square-offset check and the radius-distance check.

Hand trace: outside rectangle 40 x 20, tool diameter 6 (r = 3), climb, Control, Perpendicular lead 5, pick at (20, -5).

1. Rapid to (20, -8) at clearance, rapid to retract, plunge (feed) to Z -2.
2. Feed lead-in, centre (20, -8) to (20, -3). Programmed (20, -8) to (20, 0). G41 (climb gives `CompSide::Left`, `contour_comp.rs:331-337`) is on this linear block of 8 mm.
3. The first cut is (20, -3) toward -X (clockwise, part on the right). The control puts the centre left of the programmed edge y = 0, at y = -3.
4. The lead start is 8 mm from the wall. This is r + lead length. During the engage block the centre stays at y <= -3, so the tool edge does not cross y = 0.
5. The ring returns to (20, -3). The lead-out (20, -3) to (20, -8) carries G40. It is linear and off the part.

Pick at a corner (43, -3) or (43, 43): the seam is on the corner arc. An arc cut is refused, and so is a turn between the first and last cut (`contour_comp_pick.rs:57-71`). A seam on one chord of the corner arc is refused under Control because the nearest part point is the vertex (`contour_comp_pick.rs:84-91`). The pins are `a_compensated_pick_on_a_corner_arc_is_refused_by_name_not_moved` and `a_straight_centre_chord_over_a_part_vertex_is_refused_by_name`. The seam does not move.

Pick near an inside corner (bore, closer than r to the corner): if the projection is on the corner, the turn check refuses it (`a_compensated_pick_on_a_sharp_corner_is_refused_by_name_not_moved`). ### 4. Wear compensation

`picked_seam` gets `prog = None` for wear, so only the straight-cut and collinear checks apply. This is correct, because the programmed moves are the centre moves. The side comes from the same `side_of` as the default seam (climb gives G41, conventional gives G42). Note: a wear seam on one straight chord of an outside corner arc passes this law. The unit test shows this. It is safe because the engage and cancel offsets are on one line. The decision file records it.
